mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
Al-Ḥasan read صادِ with kasra on the dāl because of the meeting of two quiescents. It has also been said that it is an imperative of صادى يصادي, so it is an indeclinable (mabnī) imperative, like your saying رامِ زيدا and عادِ الكافر. Its meaning is then: "Confront the Qurʾān with your deeds", i.e. set your deeds against it.

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it with fatḥa on the dāl, making it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as though he said "recite Ṣād"; it is not fully declined (a diptote) because it is a definite noun, the name of the surah, so it is like a feminine noun named with "Bāb". It has also been said that the dāl (took fatḥa) because of the meeting of the two quiescents, the alif and the dāl. And it has been said that it is accusative as an oath, with the oath particle omitted, just as Sībawayh allowed اللهَ لأفعلنّ.

Ibn Abī Isḥāq read صادٍ with kasra and nunation as an oath, as you say اللهِ لأفعلنّ, making the preposition operative though it is omitted, because omission is frequent in the chapter of oaths. It has also been said that he gave it nunation only by likening it to sound-words (aṣwāt), which are nunated to distinguish the definite from the indefinite, as in إيهِ and إيهٍ, صهْ and صهٍ.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying {ولات حِين مناص}: لات, according to Sībawayh, is likened to ليس and is used only with الحين. Its ism (noun) is latent in the clause, implied and omitted, and the meaning is "and the time was not a time of escape", i.e. the moment was not a moment of flight. Sībawayh reported that some Arabs put الحين after it in the nominative and imply the khabar (predicate); this is rare.

The pause on it, according to Sībawayh, al-Farrāʾ, Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) and Ibn Kaysān, is with tāʾ; the body of readers follow this, and the script of the muṣḥaf comes with it. The pause on it according to al-Mubarrad and al-Kisāʾī is with hāʾ, like ربّه. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned that the pause is on لا, and one begins تحين مناص; this is far-fetched and contrary to the agreed-upon script of the muṣḥaf. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned that in the Imām (the ʿUthmānic master copy) it is تحين, with the tāʾ joined to the ḥāʾ.

As for the poet's saying:
.. طلبوا صلحنا ولات أوانٍ ...
("They sought peace with us, but it was no time [for it]"), which puts what follows لات in the genitive, that, according to Abū Isḥāq, is only because he meant "and our time is not a time of peace", i.e. our moment is not a moment of peace. Then the muḍāf ilayhi was dropped and (أوان) was made indeclinable; then the nunation entered as a substitute for the dropped muḍāf ilayhi, so the nūn was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents, and the nunation came to follow the kasra; it is thus like يومئذٍ and حينئذٍ. Al-Akhfash said: its implied form is "and it was not the time of a time (ولات حين أوان)", then حين was dropped. This is far-fetched; it is not permissible for the muḍāf to be dropped unless the muḍāf ilayhi takes its place in inflection, so أوان would have to be nominative. Al-Mubarrad interpreted it in this way and transmitted it in the nominative.

[Translator's note: the source reads «ثم حذف المضاف وبناه … عوضا عن المضاف المحذوف», "then the muḍāf was dropped… as a substitute for the dropped muḍāf"; the element dropped in the sense described is the muḍāf ilayhi (نا). The text also has «الأخش», evidently for «الأخفش».]

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {جند مَا هُنَالك مهزوم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); هنالك is a superfluous ẓarf (adverbial) and مَا is redundant (zāʾida). It is also possible that هنالك is the khabar and مهزوم a naʿt (adjective) of جند.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح}: the feminine marker entered كذبت only because of the femininity of the group.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying {إِذْ تسوروا}: what governs إذ is نبأ. He said تسوّروا in the plural only because الخصم is a maṣdar (verbal noun) indicating plurality, so it was put in the plural according to the sense; its implied form is "those engaged in the dispute". Likewise if you say القوم خصم, its meaning is "people engaged in a dispute". خصوم is also permissible, as you say عدول. Al-Farrāʾ said: إذ is in the sense of لمّا. What governs the second إذ is تسوّروا. It has also been said that what governs it is نبأ, on the view that the second is a clarification of what precedes it.

[Translator's note: the source is compressed here: the second إذ is in āya 22 (إذ دخلوا على داود).]

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying خصمان is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "we are two disputants".

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {الخلطاء}: the plural of خليط, like ظريف and ظرفاء. The pattern فعيل, when it is an adjective, has a plural on فُعَلاء, unless it contains a wāw, in which case it has a plural on فِعال, as in طويل and طوال.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {فغفرنا لَهُ ذَلِك}: (ذلك) is in the accusative position, governed by غفرنا, or in the nominative position by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is that".

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {الْجِيَاد}: the plural of جواد; it has also been said that it is the plural of جائد.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying {حب الْخَيْر}: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not a maṣdar (verbal noun), because he did not state that he loved with a love like the love of good things; he only stated that he preferred the love of good things. It has also been said that it is a maṣdar, but that is far-fetched in meaning.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {رَحْمَة منا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

His saying {وذكرى} is in the accusative position, conjoined to الرحمة. It has also been said that it is in the nominative position, as "and it is a reminder".

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His saying {وَاذْكُر عبادنَا إِبْرَاهِيم وَإِسْحَاق وَيَعْقُوب}: إبراهيم and what follows it are accusative as a badal (substitute) for عبادنا, so all of them are included in the servanthood and in the mention. Whoever read عبدنا in the singular made إبراهيم alone a badal for عبدنا and conjoined what follows to him; so إبراهيم is included in the servanthood and the mention, while إسحاق and يعقوب are included in the mention only — and they are included in the servanthood in other verses than this.

mekki-muskil:46-46.t:
His saying {بخالصة ذكرى الدَّار}: whoever nunated بخالصة made ذكرى a badal (substitute) for it, its implied form being "We purified them with the remembrance of the Abode"; and الدار is in the accusative position, governed by ذكرى, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is possible that ذكرى is in the accusative position, governed by خالصة, on the view that خالصة is a maṣdar like العاقبة. It is possible that (ذكرى be) accusative by خالصة on the view that خالصة is a maṣdar like العاقبة. And it is possible that ذكرى is in the nominative position, governed by خالصة. Whoever put خالصة in construct with ذكرى, it is possible for ذكرى to be in the accusative or nominative position.

[Translator's note: the second "it is possible…" sentence is a repetition in the source, translated as written.]

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {الأخيار}: the plural of خَيْر, and خَيْر is lightened from خَيِّر, like ميْت and ميِّت.

mekki-muskil:50-50.t: His saying {جنَّات عدن}: جنات is accusative as a badal (substitute) for لحسن مآب, and مفتّحة is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات. The implied form according to the Basrans is "opened for them, the gates of them". Al-Farrāʾ said the implied form is "opened for them, its gates", so the alif and lām for him are a substitute for the omitted pronoun referring back to the thing described; if you bring the pronoun, you drop them. This is not permissible according to the Basrans, because a particle cannot be a substitute for a noun. Al-Farrāʾ allowed الأبواب to be accusative, governed by مفتحة, with a pronoun for the gardens implied in مفتحة.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {هَذَا فليذوقوه حميم}: هذا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and حميم its khabar (predicate). It has also been said that فليذوقوه is the khabar of هذا, the fāʾ entering because of the drawing of attention (tanbīh) in هذا; and حميم is nominative on the implied form "this is boiling water". It has also been said that هذا is nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the matter is this", and حميم is nominative as "it is boiling water". It has also been said its implied form is "of it is boiling water". It is also possible that هذا is in the accusative position, governed by يذوقوه, with the fāʾ redundant (zāʾida), like your saying هذا زيدا فاضرب. Were it not for the fāʾ, the accusative would be preferred, because it is an imperative and so more suited to the verb; and it is permissible even so.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t:
His saying {وَآخر من شكله أَزوَاج}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); من شكله is an adjective of أُخَر, and that is why beginning with an indefinite noun is good, since it has been described. The hāʾ in شكله refers to the sense, i.e. "and others of the kind of what We have mentioned"; it has also been said that it refers to الحميم.

Whoever read وآخَر in the singular also puts it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; أزواج is a second mubtadaʾ, من شكله the khabar of أزواج, and the clause the khabar of آخر. It would not be good for أزواج to be the khabar of آخر, because a plural cannot be the khabar of a singular. It has also been said that آخر is an adjective of an omitted noun which is the mubtadaʾ, with the khabar omitted, its implied form being "and they have another punishment of the type of what preceded", and you put أزواج in the nominative by the ẓarf, namely من شكله.

This is not good in the reading of whoever read وأُخَر in the plural, because if you put أزواج in the nominative by the ẓarf, there would be no pronoun in the ẓarf, while it is an adjective, and an adjective must have a pronoun referring back to what it describes. So (that pronoun) would be nominative by the ẓarf, and a ẓarf does not put two agents in the nominative.

mekki-muskil:62-62.t: His saying ما لنا لا نرى: مَا is an interrogative mubtadaʾ (subject) and لنا the khabar (predicate); لا نرى is in the accusative position as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in لنا.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t: His saying أتخذناهم: whoever read it as a statement (اتّخذناهم) implies an interrogative to which أم is the counterpart, its implied form being "are they missing, or have our eyes swerved from them?". It is also possible that أم is the counterpart of مَا in His saying ما لنا لا نرى, because أم only comes as the counterpart of an interrogative; this has been said. Whoever read it in interrogative form makes أم its counterpart, or the counterpart of an implied (interrogative) as in the first (view). It is also possible that أم is the counterpart of مَا in both views together. Allah the Exalted said {مَا لي لَا أرى الهدهد أم كَانَ من الغائبين}, and said {مَا لكم كَيفَ تحكمون أم لكم}. And أم has occurred as the counterpart of من: Allah the Exalted said {فَمن يُجَادِل الله عَنْهُم يَوْم الْقِيَامَة أم من يكون}.

mekki-muskil:64-64.t: His saying {إِن ذَلِك لحق تخاصم}: حق is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; تخاصم is nominative on the implied form "it is the disputing". It has also been said that it is a badal (substitute) for حق; it has been said that it is a khabar after a khabar of إنّ; and it has been said that it is a badal for ذلك according to its position.

mekki-muskil:70-70.t: His saying إلا أنما: أنّ is in the nominative position, governed by يوحى, as the object whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). It has also been said that it is in the accusative position by omission of the preposition, i.e. "it is revealed to me that…" (بأنما) or "because…" (لأنما), with إليّ standing in place of the agent of يوحى. The first is better.

mekki-muskil:84-84.t: His saying {قَالَ فَالْحق وَالْحق أَقُول}: the first الحق is accusative by incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "follow the truth", or "hear the truth", or "hold to the truth". It has also been said that it is accusative as an oath, as you say اللهَ لأفعلنّ, putting it in the accusative when you have dropped the preposition; what shows that it is an oath is His saying لأملأنّ. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ and others. Whoever put the first in the nominative made it the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "I am the Truth", as He said {ثمَّ ردوا إِلَى الله مَوْلَاهُم الْحق}. It has also been said that it is a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar, its implied form being "the truth is from Me", as He said {الْحق من رَبك}. The second الحق is accusative, governed by أقول.
